newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL key share index ends down 2.39 pct, off lows.
newsitem.headline: KL key share index ends down 2.39 pct, off lows.

text.p: A plunge in big capitalised stocks pushed the key Malaysian stock market barometer to a new one-and-a-half-year low at the close.
The Composite Index closed down 2.39 percent or 24.72 points at 1,008.52. The second board index dropped 2.06 percent to 530.72 points.
"There has been fierce program selling today," said the vice president of futures at a large local brokerage house.
"There has been no impact from (Economic Advisor to the Government) Tun Daim (Zainuddin's) comments from this morning," he added.
Daim, an astute investor with a wide following in the retail market, said prices were low enough to start buying.

Worries over rising domestic interest rates and possible ringgit volatility added to recent shifting out of funds to more attractive regional markets, and spillover from the Thai baht crisis and the Cambodian clashes, they said.
Analysts said the index looked weak technically and may fall further in coming days.

"(A rebound) is less likely to happen soon in Malaysia. It looks to me as though we're going down to about 960," John Schofield, regional technical analyst at Nava SC Securities in Hong Kong told Reuters Financial Television.
Market heavyweights Telekom, Tenaga and Maybank fell between 20 and 40 cents.
Stockbrokers and fund managers said foreign funds were likely to continue trimming their Kuala Lumpur portfolios to more attractive markets in the region.
"I think it's mainly because of divided attention in the region. A lot of foreigners are probably looking at Thailand, Indonesia," said Haizan Johari, investment manager at KL Mutual Fund.
Volume was 264.52 million shares against against 256 million on Wednesday. Losers swamped gainers 664 to 49.
